modules.name: Position-Based Routing
modules.description: Native DESERT position-based routing, without global ground truth. Anchors are stationary drones that know only their own surveyed position and their own tables; a vehicle knows only its own position (from its own fix) and the surveyed positions of the anchors, and sends to the nearest anchor. Anchors estimate the vehicle position from the headers of received packets and reach it directly when the estimate is within range, otherwise through the table.
modules.reason: Verified with native bridge tests (next hop following the vehicle, native discard out of range, roles and ranges in the objects), with HoloOcean end to end (a vehicle moving away from an anchor: direct paths, then through the other anchor) and in the Network Designer (2026-10-23).

parameters.label: Anchor range
parameters.help: Distance within which an anchor sends directly to the vehicle, compared with its estimate of the vehicle position (maxTxRange_ of Module/UW/PosBasedRt); beyond it, the forwarding table is used.
parameters.constraint: positive value

parameters.label: Vehicle range
parameters.help: The vehicle sends to the nearest surveyed anchor if it is within this distance of its own position (maxTxRange_ of Module/UW/PosBasedRt/ROV); otherwise the native module discards the packet.
parameters.constraint: positive value

modules.official_example: library load only; full scheduler example not executed
modules.compatibility_reason: Verified with CSMA-ALOHA, the analytical acoustic medium and one interface per drone. Anchors have no waypoints; the vehicle estimate is the last position received (“hold” model).

modules.reason: Verified with native bridge tests, with HoloOcean end to end and in the Network Designer (Playwright tests, 2026-10-22). Also configurable from YAML and the Python API. Combinations with every MAC, routing and medium listed in compatibility verified with real delivery in DESERT (tests/integration/test_compatibility_matrix.py, 2026-10-22).
modules.official_example: library load verified; scheduler scenario not executed

flow_parameters.label: Native packet
flow_parameters.help: packetSize_ of the native model; distinct from the JSON payload and the PHY bits.

flow_parameters.label: VBR second interval
flow_parameters.help: Interval between packets in the second state of the native UW/VBR timer (the first state uses the flow interval).

flow_parameters.label: VBR first-state duration
flow_parameters.help: Duration of the first state of the native UW/VBR timer before switching to the second.

flow_parameters.label: VBR second-state duration
flow_parameters.help: Duration of the second state of the native UW/VBR timer before returning to the first.

modules.name: CS-Burst
modules.description: Channel sensing and native burst transmission; no ALOHA ACK.

parameters.label: Packets per burst
parameters.help: Native maximum number of frames sent consecutively after sensing.

parameters.label: Fixed sensing
parameters.help: Fixed part of the sensing before the burst.

parameters.label: Random sensing
parameters.help: Random component of the native sensing.

parameters.label: MAC buffer
parameters.help: Native queue limit in packets, set before construction where needed.
parameters.default_origin: verified native binding; bridge initialization profile, not a recommended operating range

modules.official_example: load sequence only; scheduler run not verified

modules.name: Ranging TokenBus
modules.description: Native token ring with timeout-based recovery. Produces estimated travel times, kept separate from the HoloOcean ground truth.

parameters.label: Token timeout
parameters.help: Native token wait timeout. It must cover airtime and propagation; it is not a TDMA slot.

parameters.label: Minimum token holding time
parameters.help: Minimum time before passing the token.

parameters.label: Maximum token holding time
parameters.help: The frame must fit within this time; the builder rejects flows that do not fit.
parameters.constraint: not less than the minimum time; it must fit the longest frame

parameters.label: MAC buffer
parameters.help: Native queue limit in packets, set before construction where needed.
parameters.default_origin: verified native binding; bridge initialization profile, not a recommended operating range

modules.official_example: load sequence only; scheduler run not verified

modules.name: Ranging TDMA
modules.description: Native TDMA that measures times of flight: in every slot the drone first sends a ranging frame and then data. Each drone estimates all pairs, from direct measurements and values received from the others; estimates are kept separate from the HoloOcean ground truth.
modules.reason: Verified with native bridge tests (data delivery, estimates for all pairs within 1 cm, update after a movement, restart) and with HoloOcean end to end up to the dashboard (2026-10-22).
modules.official_example: official sample run in a disposable container (5 nodes, exit 0); bridge chain verified separately

parameters.label: Frame duration
parameters.help: Shared cycle: each drone has a slot of length frame / number of drones, in the order of the drones in the scenario.
parameters.constraint: divided by the number of drones, it must fit the ranging frame, the data frame and the guard time

parameters.label: Guard time
parameters.help: Margin at the end of the slot. To keep adjacent slots from overlapping it should cover the longest propagation delay (distance / sound speed).
parameters.constraint: shorter than one slot

parameters.label: Transmissions per slot
parameters.help: Native transmissions per slot: the first is always the ranging frame, the others are data.
parameters.constraint: at least 2, because one transmission is the ranging frame

parameters.label: MAC buffer
parameters.help: Native queue limit in packets, set before construction where needed.
parameters.default_origin: verified native binding; bridge initialization profile, not a recommended operating range

fixed_stack.traffic_source: Python application injector; network entirely native DESERT
fixed_stack.addressing: unicast application destinations; native Flooding uses broadcast forwarding, no group multicast API

medium.label: Technology
medium.help: Native PHY, propagation and channel chain. Acoustic: DESERT BPSK; optical: Lambert-Beer with tabulated noise; electromagnetic: SF7 error table. Units and parameters change with the technology.
medium.constraint: optical and EM are verified with CSMA-ALOHA and static routing, without multi-PHY, WOSS or per-drone acoustic overrides; optical only between 0 and 20 m depth

propagation.label: Acoustic propagation
propagation.help: DESERT analytical model, or real Bellhop with a configured synthetic environment.
propagation.constraint: WOSS requires the original BPSK PHY on every drone, no multi-PHY, at least 1 m of horizontal separation and drones at least 0.1 m from the surface and the seabed

ssp.label: Sound speed profile
ssp.help: Sound speed profile read by Bellhop: depth/speed pairs in increasing depth order.
ssp.constraint: 2 to 256 points; the first at 0 m, the last at the seabed depth; speeds between 1000 and 2000 m/s

multiphy.label: Multiple interfaces (multi-PHY)
multiphy.help: Each drone has 2 or 3 interfaces, acoustic or optical, under a single MAC; the native DESERT controller chooses the active interface.
multiphy.constraint: analytical propagation only, CSMA-ALOHA without ACK and static routing; acoustic interface bands must be disjoint

multiphy_interface.label: Interface
multiphy_interface.help: Interface name (lowercase letters, digits, _). Empty fields inherit the global parameters of its medium (acoustic channel or optical parameters).
multiphy_interface.constraint: 2 to 3 interfaces with unique names; the bands of the acoustic interfaces must not overlap

multiphy_policy.label: Interface selection
multiphy_policy.help: Manual: the application chooses with select_interface (Python API). Received power: the native master/slave controller switches interface according to the measured power.
multiphy_policy.constraint: received-power selection requires every interface on every drone and thresholds between adjacent interfaces

multiphy_initial.label: Initial interface
multiphy_initial.help: Interface active at start-up on every drone.
multiphy_initial.constraint: must be available on every drone

multiphy_master.label: Master drone
multiphy_master.help: Drone that measures the power and decides the switch; the others follow as slaves.

multiphy_alpha.label: Averaging weight (alpha)
multiphy_alpha.help: Weight of the new sample in the master's exponential average of the received power.

multiphy_threshold.label: Received-power threshold
multiphy_threshold.unit: linear units of the acoustic PHY (µPa²) or W
multiphy_threshold.help: The master compares the average received power Pr on the current interface: it switches to the next interface when Pr exceeds the threshold and to the previous one when Pr falls below it. The threshold is in the PHY unit of the interface being left: Pr = 10^(received level/10) for an acoustic interface, W for an optical interface.
multiphy_threshold.constraint: positive value; both directions between adjacent interfaces are needed

multiphy_available.label: Interfaces available per drone
multiphy_available.constraint: the initial interface is mandatory; received-power selection needs all of them

generator.label: Generator
generator.help: Python: application messages with envelope and TTL. CBR/VBR: timers and packets generated by the native DESERT modules, with neither envelope nor TTL.
generator.constraint: native generators accept only data messages, periodic or Poisson timing, no replies and no final interval

multiphy_medium.label: Medium
multiphy_medium.help: Acoustic: BPSK PHY on the shared acoustic channel, power in dB re 1 µPa. Optical: native DESERT optical PHY (UW/OPTICAL) on a separate optical channel, Lambert-Beer propagation, power in W; range of a few metres to a few tens of metres.
multiphy_medium.constraint: an optical interface requires drones between 0 and 20 m depth (optical noise table); with received-power selection, optical interfaces come after the acoustic ones

position_based_anchors.label: Position-based routing anchors
position_based_anchors.help: An anchor is a stationary drone: the routing knows only its surveyed position (empty: the scenario position) and its forwarding table. The other drones are vehicles and know only their own position and the surveyed positions of the anchors.
position_based_anchors.constraint: at least one anchor and one vehicle; anchors have no waypoints; tables list only anchors, with an anchor or the destination as next hop
